parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were university professors in physics and mathematics, providing a deeply academic environment and direct scientific domain exposure from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: professor parents, IMO gold medals, French mathematical pipeline, Laumon mentorship, Fundamental Lemma, Fields Medal
evidence_summary: Chau was born in Hanoi to a physics professor father and a mathematics professor mother. He won two IMO gold medals (1988, 1989), studied at the Ecole Normale Superieure in Paris, and completed his PhD at Universite Paris-Sud at 25 under Gerard Laumon. His parents' academic background and the elite French mathematical pipeline were key advantages. He later proved the Fundamental Lemma, winning the Fields Medal.
starting_point: Born in Hanoi, Vietnam to a physics professor father and a mathematics professor mother at Vietnam National University; raised in an academic household with strong mathematical and scientific traditions.
current_position: Professor of Mathematics at the University of Chicago; Fields Medalist (2010); permanent member of the Institute for Advanced Study.

trajectory.description: Admitted to the elite Ecole Normale Superieure in Paris on a French government scholarship.

trajectory.description: Earned his doctorate under Gerard Laumon, working on the automorphic forms and the Langlands program.

trajectory.title: Published proof of Fundamental Lemma
trajectory.description: Completed the proof of the Fundamental Lemma, a key conjecture in the Langlands program that had resisted solution for decades.

trajectory.title: Awarded Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Received the Fields Medal at the ICM in Hyderabad for his proof of the Fundamental Lemma, becoming the first Vietnamese-born mathematician to receive the honor.

trajectory.description: Appointed as a professor of mathematics at the University of Chicago.
